title: MPSNet Sits Down with Chairman mike0w73 and Chief Instructor Policeswat8934dudess
author: MPSNet
excerpt: MPSNet interviewed Major General mike0w73 and Colonel Policeswat8934dudess about the state of the Military Police School, its Instructors, MIDCOM, and the Marines who may want to join.
imageCaption: MPSNet interview at the Military Police School

body.text: MPSNet, the news channel of the Military Police School, recently sat down with two of the most senior figures in the school for a pair of interviews on where MPS stands today. Both conversations were led by MPSNet reporter 65VI9 and covered the overall state of the school, the work of its Instructors and MIDCOM, and the message each leader has for the Marines who may want to join.

The first interview was held with Major General mike0w73, Chairman of the Military Police School and the highest ranking member of HICOM. The second was held with Colonel Policeswat8934dudess, Chief Instructor, who sits in the Middle Command and sees the daily running of the school from the Instructor side. Together, the two interviews give a view of MPS from the top of the chain and from the training floor.
Interview with the Chairman
Chairman mike0w73 was first asked the question on the mind of every member of the school: how is MPS doing right now? The answer was direct and built around one word, activity.

body.q: What do you think about the current state of Military Police School?
body.a: Well, the current state of MPS, for me, is very active recently. As the backbone of all MPs, we always have to be active for every type of issue or anything that we may face.

body.text: As the backbone of all MPs, we always have to be active for every type of issue or anything that we may face.
body.by: Major General mike0w73, Chairman of MPS

body.text: Describing MPS as the backbone of all MPs sets the tone for the rest of the Chairman's interview. A school that trains and supports the wider Military Police community cannot afford to slow down, because the issues it meets can come from any direction at any time. The Chairman's assessment is that the school has been meeting that standard recently.
On the Instructors
Instructors are the face of MPS to every Marine who goes through training, so the Chairman was asked for an honest view of them.

body.q: What do you think about the Instructors?
body.a:
The Instructors, just like MIDCOM, are doing great work and I am really proud of it. I have seen some Instructors who caught my attention because they are good at their work.
I am very proud of them.

body.text: The Chairman placed the Instructors in the same category as MIDCOM and praised both for the work they are putting in. The Chairman also pointed out that a few Instructors have personally caught their attention because of how well they do their jobs, a remark that suggests HICOM is paying close attention to the work being done on the ground.
A Message to Future Members
To close the interview, MPSNet asked whether the Chairman had anything to say to Marine Personnel who are thinking about joining the Military Police School. The reply was an open invitation.

body.q: Do you have any words to send to the Marine Personnel who want to join the MPS?
body.a: If someone likes to make and instruct future leaders, please come to MPS. We will receive you with open arms and make you feel at home.

body.text: We will receive you with open arms and make you feel at home.
body.by: Major General mike0w73, Chairman of MPS

body.text: The message was aimed at a specific kind of Marine: someone who enjoys teaching and wants to help shape the next generation of leaders. For anyone who fits that description, the Chairman made it clear that the door of MPS is open. MPSNet thanked the Chairman for their time and for taking part in the interview.
Interview with the Chief Instructor

Shortly after, MPSNet spoke with Colonel Policeswat8934dudess, Chief Instructor of the Military Police School. Asked whether they were free for a fast interview, the Colonel agreed, and the conversation started with the same question that opened the Chairman's interview.

body.q: What do you think about the status of MPS?
body.a: It is doing quite well with the new leadership of Chairman, O8 Mike, Vice Chairman, O7 Ags_Xfang, Division Sergeant Major, E9B Anthony, and ADC, O6 65VI9. However, in my opinion, the activity of MA is quite low, which leads to MPS being inactive sometimes.

body.text: The Chief Instructor gave a balanced assessment. On the positive side, the Colonel credited the current leadership team for the way the school is doing, naming the Chairman, the Vice Chairman, the Division Sergeant Major, and Aide-de-Camp 65VI9, who was recently appointed to the role and is also the MPSNet reporter conducting these interviews.

On the other side, the Colonel was candid about one area that needs work. In the Chief Instructor's view, the activity of MA is quite low, and that is what leads to MPS going quiet at times. It was a short remark, but it points to a clear target for the school going forward.
On the Instructors and MIDCOM

body.q: What do you think about its Instructors?
body.a: I think the Instructors are doing a wonderful job carrying out their duties, and they are very active when it comes to hosting phases.

body.text: As a Chief Instructor, Colonel Policeswat8934dudess works closely with the Instructor team, which gives extra weight to this praise. The Colonel specifically highlighted how active the Instructors are when it comes to hosting phases, one of the most visible parts of life at MPS.

body.q: What do you think about MIDCOMs?
body.a: The MIDCOMs are wonderful. They are doing a great job in the communication between HICOM and the Instructors, and they are also doing a wonderful job in increasing the activity of MPS.

body.text: The Colonel described MIDCOM as the link between HICOM and the Instructors, a role that keeps decisions from the top and feedback from the floor moving in both directions. According to the Chief Instructor, MIDCOM is also helping to raise the overall activity of the school.
Two Leaders, One Common Theme

Although the two interviews were held separately, both leaders returned to the same word: activity. The Chairman sees MPS as very active at the moment and expects the school to stay that way for every issue it may face. The Chief Instructor agrees that the school is doing well, while noting that activity, especially from MA, is what decides whether MPS stays busy or goes quiet.

Both leaders were also united in their praise for the Instructors and for MIDCOM, the people who carry out the daily work of training and communication inside the school. For members who have been putting in the effort, the message from the top of the Military Police School is that the work is noticed and appreciated.
MPSNet thanks Major General mike0w73 and Colonel Policeswat8934dudess for taking the time to speak with us.
